{"file_path":"src/Gateway.sol","creation_status":"success","source_code":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: BUSL-1.1\npragma solidity ^0.8.25;\n\nimport {Step, Path, FundingEntry, SubmitterInputs, ExecutionContext} from \"./types/Common.sol\";\nimport {GatewayContext} from \"./modules/GatewayContext.sol\";\nimport {StepLib, PathLib} from \"./libraries/GatewayIds.sol\";\nimport {IGateway} from \"./interfaces/IGateway.sol\";\nimport {IAcrossV5Executor} from \"./interfaces/IAcrossV5Executor.sol\";\nimport {GatewayFunding} from \"./modules/GatewayFunding.sol\";\nimport {Bytes32ToAddress} from \"./libraries/external/AddressConverters.sol\";\nimport {MerkleProof} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/cryptography/MerkleProof.sol\";\nimport {UUPSUpgradeable} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts-upgradeable/proxy/utils/UUPSUpgradeable.sol\";\nimport {OwnableUpgradeable} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts-upgradeable/access/OwnableUpgradeable.sol\";\n\n/// @title Gateway\n/// @notice Single upgradeable entry point for all Across V5 step submissions.\n///         Calculates stepId, resolves the concrete Path via Merkle proof,\n///         routes funding entries to the execution target, and invokes it.\ncontract Gateway is GatewayContext, GatewayFunding, UUPSUpgradeable, OwnableUpgradeable {\n    using StepLib for Step;\n    using PathLib for Path;\n\n    /// @custom:oz-upgrades-unsafe-allow constructor\n    constructor(address permit2_, address multicall3_) GatewayFunding(permit2_, multicall3_) {\n        _disableInitializers();\n    }\n\n    function initialize(address owner_) external initializer {\n        __Ownable_init(owner_);\n        __GatewayFunding_init();\n    }\n\n    /// @inheritdoc IGateway\n    function execute(Step step, SubmitterInputs calldata submitterInputs, FundingEntry[] calldata funding)\n        external\n        payable\n        override\n    {\n        // A non-zero submitter means an execution is in flight; the context doubles as the reentrancy guard.\n        if (currentSubmitter() != address(0)) revert Reentrancy();\n\n        bytes32 stepId = step.id();\n        Path calldata path = submitterInputs.path;\n        if (path.chainId != block.chainid) revert WrongChain(path.chainId, block.chainid);\n        bytes32 pathId = path.id();\n        if (!MerkleProof.verify(submitterInputs.proof, stepId, pathId)) revert InvalidMerkleProof();\n\n        _setExecutionContext(ExecutionContext(stepId, pathId, msg.sender, path.salt));\n\n        address executor = Bytes32ToAddress.toAddress(path.executor);\n        // Funding loop: untrusted tokens may get control here. `currentExecutor()` is\n        // still zero, so funding adapters (which require `msg.sender == currentExecutor()`)\n        // cannot be triggered by a reentrant hook before the user's command tape runs.\n        for (uint256 i; i < funding.length; ++i) {\n            _pullFunding(stepId, funding[i], executor);\n        }\n\n        // Executor call: the user's command tape (and its BALANCE_REQ guards) controls flow.\n        // `currentExecutor()` is live only for the duration of this call.\n        // Future: dispatch a limited Gateway-native command set when `executor == address(this)`,\n        // letting commands route funding directly without an external executor hop.\n        _setExecutor(executor);\n        IAcrossV5Executor(executor).executeAcrossV5{value: address(this).balance}(\n            path.message, submitterInputs.executorMessage\n        );\n        _setExecutor(address(0));\n\n        _setExecutionContext(ExecutionContext(bytes32(0), bytes32(0), address(0), bytes32(0)));\n\n        emit StepExecuted(stepId, pathId, msg.sender);\n    }\n\n    // UUPS\n    function _authorizeUpgrade(address) internal override onlyOwner {}\n}\n","deployed_bytecode":"","optimization_enabled":true,"verified_twin_address_hash":null,"is_verified":true,"compiler_settings":{"evmVersion":"prague","libraries":{},"metadata":{"appendCBOR":false,"bytecodeHash":"none","useLiteralContent":false},"optimizer":{"enabled":true,"runs":2000000},"outputSelection":{"*":{"":["*"],"*":["*"]}},"remappings":["forge-std/=lib/forge-std/src/","across-contracts/=lib/across-contracts/contracts/","@openzeppelin/contracts/=lib/openzeppelin-contracts/contracts/","@openzeppelin/contracts-upgradeable/=lib/openzeppelin-contracts-upgradeable/contracts/","murky/=lib/murky/","@across-contracts/=lib/across-contracts/contracts/","@across-protocol/=lib/across-contracts/node_modules/@across-protocol/","@ensdomains/=lib/across-contracts/node_modules/@ensdomains/","@eth-optimism/=lib/across-contracts/node_modules/@eth-optimism/","@gnosis.pm/=lib/across-contracts/node_modules/@gnosis.pm/","@maticnetwork/=lib/across-contracts/node_modules/@maticnetwork/","@matterlabs/=lib/across-contracts/node_modules/@matterlabs/","@scroll-tech/=lib/across-contracts/node_modules/@scroll-tech/","@sp1-contracts/=lib/across-contracts/lib/sp1-contracts/contracts/","@uniswap/=lib/across-contracts/node_modules/@uniswap/","arb-bridge-eth/=lib/across-contracts/node_modules/arb-bridge-eth/","arb-bridge-peripherals/=lib/across-contracts/node_modules/arb-bridge-peripherals/","arbos-precompiles/=lib/across-contracts/node_modules/arbos-precompiles/","base64-sol/=lib/across-contracts/node_modules/base64-sol/","ds-test/=lib/murky/lib/openzeppelin-contracts/lib/forge-std/lib/ds-test/src/","erc4626-tests/=lib/openzeppelin-contracts-upgradeable/lib/erc4626-tests/","eth-gas-reporter/=lib/across-contracts/node_modules/eth-gas-reporter/","halmos-cheatcodes/=lib/openzeppelin-contracts-upgradeable/lib/halmos-cheatcodes/src/","hardhat-deploy/=lib/across-contracts/node_modules/hardhat-deploy/","hardhat/=lib/across-contracts/node_modules/hardhat/","openzeppelin-contracts-upgradeable/=l used by Gateway.\ninterface IPermit2 {\n    struct TokenPermissions {\n        address token;\n        uint256 amount;\n    }\n\n    struct PermitTransferFrom {\n        TokenPermissions permitted;\n permitWitnessTransferFrom(\n        PermitTransferFrom memory permit,\n        SignatureTransferDetails calldata transferDetails,\n        address owner,\n        bytes32 witness,\n        string calldata witnessTypeString,\n        bytes calldata signature\n    ) external;\n}\n"},{"file_path":"src/modules/GatewayFunding.sol","source_code":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: BUSL-1.1\npragma solidity ^0.8.25;\n\nimport {IGateway} from \"../interfaces/IGateway.sol\";\nimport {IPermit2} from \"../interfaces/external/IPermit2.sol\";\nimport {IEIP3009} from \"../interfaces/external/IEIP3009.sol\";\nimport {FundingCodec} from \"../libraries/FundingCodec.sol\";\nimport {ERC6492MemorySignatureHandler} from \"../libraries/ERC6492MemorySignatureHandler.sol\";\nimport {FundingEntry} from \"../types/Common.sol\";\n\nimport {IERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/IERC20.sol\";\nimport {IERC20Permit} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/extensions/IERC20Permit.sol\";\nimport {SafeERC20} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/utils/SafeERC20.sol\";\nimport {ECDSA} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/cryptography/ECDSA.sol\";\nimport {EIP712Upgradeable} from \"@openzeppelin/contracts-upgradeable/utils/cryptography/EIP712Upgradeable.sol\";\nimport {SafeTransferERC20} from \"across-contracts/libraries/SafeTransferERC20.sol\";\n\n//  Funding type constants (funding entry typ)\nuint8 constant FUNDING_TRANSFER_FROM = 1;\nuint8 constant FUNDING_PERMIT2_WITNESS = 2;\n// Canonical EIP-3009 ECDSA path: data carries (v, r, s) directly, dispatched\n// to the (v, r, s) overload of `receiveWithAuthorization`.\nuint8 constant FUNDING_EIP3009 = 3;\n// EIP-3009 with arbitrary-length signature: data carries `bytes signature`,\n// dispatched to the `bytes signature` overload (FiatTokenV2_2+ / EIP-1271).\n// The signature may be ERC-6492 wrapped for counterfactual contract-wallet signers.\nuint8 constant FUNDING_EIP3009_BYTES = 4;\nuint8 constant FUNDING_ERC2612_PERMIT = 5;\nuint8 constant FUNDING_SIGNED_TRANSFER_FROM = 6;\n\n/// @title GatewayFunding\n/// @notice Funding portion of the Gateway. Owns the Permit2 reference and the\n///         authorization replay ledger, and dispatches each `FundingEntry` to\n///         transfer funds directly to the Gateway-selected recipient.\n/// @dev Inherits `ERC6492MemorySignatureHandler` so the `bytes signature` funding paths\n///      (Permit2 witness and EIP-3009 bytes) additionally accept ERC-6492 wrapped\n///      signatures from counterfactual (not-yet-deployed) contract wallets: the\n///      wrapped factory call deploys the signer before the downstream verifier\n///      (Permit2 or the token) runs its EIP-1271 check. The handler is stateless\n///      (immutable only), so inheriting it does not affect the upgradeable\n///      storage layout.\nabstract contract GatewayFunding is EIP712Upgradeable, SafeTransferERC20, ERC6492MemorySignatureHandler {\n    // Restricted to exclude `safeTransfer`: ERC20 transfers out of the Gateway must go\n    // through the overridable `_safeTransfer` hook (see `SafeTransferERC20`), so chain\n    // variants (e.g. Tron) can swap the transfer semantics in one place. `SafeTransferERC20`\n    // is stateless, so inheriting it does not affect the upgradeable storage layout.\n    using {SafeERC20.safeTransferFrom} for IERC20;\n\n    string internal constant PERMIT2_WITNESS_TYPE_STRING =\n        \"bytes32 witness)TokenPermissions(address token,uint256 amount)\";\n\n    /// @custom:oz-upgrades-unsafe-allow state-variable-immutable\n    IPermit2 public immutable permit2;\n\n    /// @dev Single ERC-7201 namespace for all funding-module storage.\n    /// @custom:storage-location erc7201:acxv.gateway.funding\n    struct FundingStorage {\n        mapping(bytes32 structHash => bool used) signedTransferAuthUsed;\n    }\n\n    // keccak256(abi.encode(uint256(keccak256(\"acxv.gateway.funding\")) - 1)) & ~bytes32(uint256(0xff))\n    bytes32 private constant FUNDING_STORAGE_LOCATION =\n        0xb14f74039aa76b5912eee397f92ab1c702ee124a803365d3213dfc2ec8bffe00;\n\n    function _fundingStorage() private pure returns (FundingStorage storage $) {\n        assembly {\n            $.slot := FUNDING_STORAGE_LOCATION\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// @dev EIP-712 type for `FUNDING_SIGNED_TRANSFER_FROM` authorizations.\n    ///      The witness is always the current stepId, binding the pull to a\n    ///      specific Gateway execution scope.\n    bytes32 internal constant SIGNED_TRANSFER_FROM_TYPEHASH =\n        keccak256(\"SignedTransferFrom(address from,address token,uint256 amount,uint32 deadline,bytes32 witness)\");\n\n    /// @notice Whether a signed-transferFrom authorization with the given EIP-712\n    ///         struct hash has been consumed. Useful for off-chain replay checks.\n    function isSignedTransferAuthUsed(bytes32 structHash) external view returns (bool) {\n        return _fundingStorage().signedTransferAuthUsed[structHash];\n    }\n\n    /// @custom:oz-upgrades-unsafe-allow constructor\n    constructor(address permit2_, address multicall3_) ERC6492MemorySignatureHandler(multicall3_) {\n        permit2 = IPermit2(permit2_);\n    }\n\n    function __GatewayFunding_init() internal onlyInitializing {\n        __EIP712_init(\"Gateway\", \"1\");\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Resolve one funding entry, routing the underlying transfer to `to`.\n    ///      Witness-bound funding always uses the current stepId.\n    function _pullFunding(bytes32 stepId, FundingEntry calldata entry, address to) internal {\n        uint8 typ = FundingCodec.unpackHeader(entry.header);\n\n        if (typ == FUNDING_TRANSFER_FROM) {\n            _pullTransferFrom(entry.data, to);\n        } else if (typ == FUNDING_ERC2612_PERMIT) {\n            _runERC2612Permit(entry.data);\n        } else {\n            if (typ == FUNDING_PERMIT2_WITNESS) {\n                _pullPermit2Witness(stepId, entry.data, to);\n            } else if (typ == FUNDING_EIP3009) {\n                _pullEIP3009(stepId, entry.data, to);\n            } else if (typ == FUNDING_EIP3009_BYTES) {\n                _pullEIP3009Bytes(stepId, entry.data, to);\n            } else if (typ == FUNDING_SIGNED_TRANSFER_FROM) {\n                _pullSignedTransferFrom(stepId, entry.data, to);\n            } else {\n                revert IGateway.UnknownFundingType(typ);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Allowance-based ERC-20 transferFrom. Only the from themselves may trigger this.\n    ///      This keeps Gateway safely approveable: a third-party submitter cannot spend\n    ///      another account's plain ERC-20 allowance without that account being the direct caller.\n    function _pullTransferFrom(bytes calldata data, address to) internal {\n        (address token, uint256 amount) = FundingCodec.decodeTokenAmount(data);\n        IERC20(token).safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, to, amount);\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Permit2 single-token witness transfer. The signature may be ERC-6492\n    ///      wrapped: the embedded factory call is executed first (deploying a\n    ///      counterfactual contract-wallet signer) before Permit2 verifies the\n    ///      unwrapped inner signature via EIP-1271.\n    function _pullPermit2Witness(bytes32 witness, bytes calldata data, address to) internal {\n        (address from, IPermit2.PermitTransferFrom memory permitData, bytes memory signature) =\n            abi.decode(data, (address, IPermit2.PermitTransferFrom, bytes));\n\n        IPermit2.SignatureTransferDetails memory details =\n            IPermit2.SignatureTransferDetails({to: to, requestedAmount: permitData.permitted.amount});\n\n        permit2.permitWitnessTransferFrom(\n            permitData, details, from, witness, PERMIT2_WITNESS_TYPE_STRING, _handleERC6492SignatureMemory(signature)\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// @dev EIP-3009 ReceiveWithAuthorization, canonical `(v, r, s)` overload.\n    ///      Compatible with vanilla ERC-3009 tokens. The Gateway is signed as the receiver — the token\n    ///      enforces `msg.sender == to`, so only this Gateway can submit the\n    ///      authorization (front-running protection). After receipt, the Gateway\n    ///      forwards the tokens to `to`.\n    function _pullEIP3009(bytes32 witness, bytes calldata data, address to) internal {\n        (\n            address from,\n            address token,\n            uint256 amount,\n            uint256 validAfter,\n            uint256 validBefore,\n            uint8 v,\n            bytes32 r,\n            bytes32 s\n        ) = abi.decode(data, (address, address, uint256, uint256, uint256, uint8, bytes32, bytes32));\n\n        IEIP3009(token).receiveWithAuthorization(from, address(this), amount, validAfter, validBefore, witness, v, r, s);\n\n        if (to != address(this)) {\n            _safeTransfer(token, to, amount);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// @dev EIP-3009 ReceiveWithAuthorization, `bytes signature` overload.\n    ///      Used for FiatTokenV2_2+ and other implementations that route the\n    ///      signature through `SignatureChecker` / EIP-1271 to support\n    ///      contract-wallet signers. Set immediately before the Gateway calls the executor\n    ///         and cleared after it returns — so it reads zero while idle AND while the funding\n    ///         loop runs (where untrusted tokens/funders may get control). Funding adapters\n    ///         authenticate their caller against this field: `msg.sender == currentExecutor()`\n    ///         proves the call comes from the live step's committed executor mid-tape.\n    function currentExecutor() external view returns (address executor_);\n\n    /// @notice The `path.salt` of the currently executing step, or bytes32(0) when idle. Exposed so a\n    ///         committed requirement/planner can authenticate values folded into the salt (e.g. the\n    ///         counterfactual destination salt preimage) without rebuilding the pathId/stepId itself.\n    function currentSalt() external view returns (bytes32 salt_);\n\n    /// @notice Execute a step in one transaction.\n    function execute(Step step, SubmitterInputs calldata submitterInputs, FundingEntry[] calldata funding)\n        external\n        payable;\n}\n"},{"file_path":"src/libraries/external/AddressConverters.sol","source_code":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: /**************************************\n     *              ERRORS                *\n     **************************************/\n    error InvalidBytes32();\n\n    function toAddress(bytes32 _bytes32) internal pure returns (address) {\n        checkAddress(_bytes32);\n        return address(uint160(uint256(_bytes32)));\n    }\n\n    function toAddressUnchecked(bytes32 _bytes32) internal pure returns (address) {\n        return address(uint160(uint256(_bytes32)));\n    }\n\n    function checkAddress(bytes32 _bytes32) internal pure {\n        if (!isValidAddress(_bytes32)) {\n            revert InvalidBytes32();\n        }\n    }\n\n    function isValidAddress(bytes32 _bytes32) internal pure returns (bool) {\n        return uint256(_bytes32) >> 160 == 0;\n    }\n}\n\nlibrary AddressToBytes32 {\n    function toBytes32(address _address) internal pure returns (bytes32) {\n        return bytes32(uint256(uint160(_address)));\n    }\n}\n"},{"file_path":"lib/openzeppelin-contracts/contracts/utils/Panic.sol","source_code":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\n// OpenZeppelin Contracts (last updated v5.1.0) (utils/Panic.sol)\n\npragma This child adds\n///      `_handleERC6492SignatureMemory` while reusing the vendored base's magic constant, `multicall3`\n///      immutable, and constructor checks. Security model is identical: the embedded factory call is\n///      attacker-controlled and is routed through the neutral Multicall3 singleton, so this contract\n///      is never the `msg.sender` of the prepare call, and failure is tolerated (already-deployed\n///      wallet); the downstream verifier remains the source of truth on signature validity.\nabstract contract ERC6492MemorySignatureHandler is ERC6492SignatureHandler {\n    /// @custom:oz-upgrades-unsafe-allow constructor\n    constructor(address _multicall3) ERC6492SignatureHandler(_multicall3) {}\n\n    /// @notice Detects an ERC-6492 wrapped signature and, if present, runs its embedded factory call\n    ///         to deploy the (counterfactual) signer before returning the unwrapped inner signature.\n    /// @param signature The user-provided signature, possibly ERC-6492 wrapped.\n    /// @return The inner signature to forward to the real verifier. If `signature` is not ERC-6492\n    ///         wrapped it is returned unchanged.\n    function _handleERC6492SignatureMemory(bytes memory signature) internal returns (bytes memory) {\n        // An ERC-6492 signature is at least the 32-byte magic suffix; anything shorter passes through.\n        uint256 signatureLength = signature.length;\n        if (signatureLength < _ERC6492_MAGIC_VALUE.length) return signature;\n\n        // Pass through unless the trailing 32 bytes are the ERC-6492 magic value.\n        bytes32 suffix;\n        assembly {\n            suffix := mload(add(signature, signatureLength))\n        }\n        if (suffix != _ERC6492_MAGIC_VALUE) return signature;\n\n        // Decode the wrapped (factory, factoryCalldata, innerSignature). The magic suffix is excluded\n        // by temporarily shortening the array's length word — abi.decode allocates fresh copies of the\n        // decoded fields — and the original length is restored afterwards.\n        assembly {\n            mstore(signature, sub(signatureLength, 32))\n        }\n        (address prepareTarget, bytes memory prepareData, bytes memory innerSignature) =\n            abi.decode(signature, (address, bytes, bytes));\n        assembly {\n            mstore(signature, signatureLength)\n        }\n\n        // Route the deploy call through the neutral Multicall3 so this contract is never the sender of\n        // attacker-controlled calldata. Failure is tolerated (e.g. the wallet is already deployed);\n        // the downstream verifier is the source of truth on signature validity.\n        IMulticall3.Call[] memory calls = new IMulticall3.Call[](1);\n        calls[0] = IMulticall3.Call(prepareTarget, prepareData);\n        multicall3.tryAggregate({requireSuccess: false, calls: calls});\n\n        return innerSignature;\n    }\n}\n"},{"file_path":"src/libraries/external/ERC6492SignatureHandler.sol","source_code":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-or-later\npragma solidity ^0.8.0;\n\nimport {IMulticall3} from \"../external/interfaces/IMulticall3.sol\";\n\n/**\n * @title ERC6492SignatureHandler\n * @notice Base contract that performs the \"prepare\" (deploy) step of an ERC-6492 signature without\n * being the signature verifier itself.\n * @dev Some downstream verifiers — the ERC-3009 `receiveWithAuthorization(...,bytes)` overload on\n * tokens such as USDC v2.2, and Uniswap's Permit2 — validate contract-wallet signatures via EIP-1271\n * but have no concept of ERC-6492. A signature from a *counterfactual* (not-yet-deployed)\n * smart-contract wallet therefore fails, because there is no code at the signer's address to call\n * `isValidSignature` on.\n *\n * ERC-6492 (https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-6492) solves this by wrapping the real signature with\n * the factory call needed to deploy the wallet. Since we cannot change the token's verification, we\n * replicate only the *deploy* half of the flow here: if a signature carries the ERC-6492 magic\n * suffix, we run its embedded factory call to materialize the wallet, then hand the unwrapped inner\n * signature back to the caller to pass on to the real verifier (the token). Once the wallet exists,\n * the token's own EIP-1271 check against the signer succeeds.\n *\n * @dev This contract does NOT validate the signature; it only ensures the signer is deployed. The\n * embedded factory `target`/`callData` is fully attacker-controlled, so the call is routed through a\n * neutral public Multicall3 singleton rather than made directly. This guarantees the prepare call can\n * never execute with this contract as `msg.sender` and thus cannot abuse any of this contract's\n * allowances or privileges. The call is made with `requireSuccess: false`, so an already-deployed\n * wallet (whose factory call reverts on redeploy) is tolerated; correctness ultimately rests on the\n * downstream verifier.\n *\n * Inspired by Coinbase's ERC6492SignatureHandler\n * (https://github.com/base/commerce-payments/blob/main/src/collectors/ERC6492SignatureHandler.sol).\n *\n * @dev Vendored as is from https://github.com/across-protocol/contracts.\n * @custom:security-contact bugs@across.to\n */\nabstract contract ERC6492SignatureHandler {\n    // Magic suffix that marks a signature as ERC-6492 wrapped.\n    bytes32 internal constant _ERC6492_MAGIC_VALUE = 0x6492649264926492649264926492649264926492649264926492649264926492;\n\n    // Canonical Multicall3 singleton used to make the neutral ERC-6492 prepare/deploy call.\n    IMulticall3 public immutable multicall3;\n\n    /**\n     * @notice Constructs the handler.\n     * @param _multicall3 Address of the canonical Multicall3 singleton used to route prepare calls.\n     */\n    constructor(address _multicall3) {\n        require(_multicall3 != address(0), \"Multicall3 cannot be zero address\");\n        require(_multicall3.code.length > 0, \"Multicall3 must be a contract\");\n        multicall3 = IMulticall3(_multicall3);\n    }\n\n    /**\n     * @notice Detects an ERC-6492 wrapped signature and, if present, runs its embedded factory call\n     * to deploy the (counterfactual) signer before returning the unwrapped inner signature.\n     * @param signature The user-provided signature, possibly ERC-6492 wrapped.\n     * @return The inner signature to forward to the real verifier. 1)) & ~bytes32(uint256(0xff))\nbytes32 constant GATEWAY_STEP_ID_SLOT = 0x874f352368d93bd514b77b44e4378927e066c259dfc0b9f467f3f857a45f5c00;\n// erc7201(\"acxv.gateway.context.pathId\")\n// = keccak256(abi.encode(uint256(keccak256(\"acxv.gateway.context.pathId\")) - 1)) & ~bytes32(uint256(0xff))\nbytes32 constant GATEWAY_PATH_ID_SLOT = 0x13ef2becd97226d4f4ec1098e178bafc164b88daa20eadf741a6be2d95da5f00;\n// erc7201(\"acxv.gateway.context.submitter\")\n// = keccak256(abi.encode(uint256(keccak256(\"acxv.gateway.context.submitter\")) - 1)) & ~bytes32(uint256(0xff))\nbytes32 constant GATEWAY_SUBMITTER_SLOT = 0x0b2d31a9dc2e90587f4a831516fafe287ec2fee415eccb0edf35638482db8600;\n// erc7201(\"acxv.gateway.context.executor\")\n// = keccak256(abi.encode(uint256(keccak256(\"acxv.gateway.context.executor\")) - 1)) & ~bytes32(uint256(0xff))\nbytes32 constant GATEWAY_EXECUTOR_SLOT = 0x99e1f0f03bd34564a8a71e6cb64f52ee3b947697d75ffa1b4c1a39363b43b700;\n// erc7201(\"acxv.gateway.context.salt\")\n// = keccak256(abi.encode(uint256(keccak256(\"acxv.gateway.context.salt\")) - 1)) & ~bytes32(uint256(0xff))\nbytes32 constant GATEWAY_SALT_SLOT = 0x491e81ebbd15122b9066297799b2e4f59e6552bf3710c94e8cd9b5c7d1efd900;\n\n/// @title GatewayContext\n/// @notice Holds the live `ExecutionContext` for the in-flight Gateway submission,\n///         backed by transient storage.\n/// @dev Inherits `IGateway` (not a smaller context-only interface) so the\n///      `currentPathId` / `currentSubmitter` implementations sit on a single\n///      linear inheritance path with `Gateway`'s `IGateway`. The set-point is what turns\n    ///      `msg.sender == currentExecutor()` into a complete funding-adapter boundary check.\n    function _setExecutor(address executor) internal virtual {\n        assembly {\n            tstore(GATEWAY_EXECUTOR_SLOT, executor)\n        }\n    }\n}\n"},{"file_path":"lib/openzeppelin-contracts/contracts/utils/Errors.sol","source_code":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\n// OpenZeppelin Contracts (last updated v5.1.0) (utils/Errors.sol)\n\npragma solidity ^0.8.20;\n\n/**\n * @dev Collection of common custom errors used in multiple contracts\n *\n * IMPORTANT: Backwards compatibility is not guaranteed in future versions of the library.\n * It is recommended to avoid relying on the error API for critical functionality.\n *\n * _Available since v5.1._\n */\nlibrary Errors {\n    /**\n     * @dev The ETH balance of the account is not enough to perform the operation.\n     */\n    error InsufficientBalance(uint256 balance, uint256 needed);\n\n    /**\n     * @dev A call to an address target failed. solidity ^0.8.25;\n\nimport {Step, Path} from \"./../types/Common.sol\";\n\n/*\n\nA system of identifying cross-chain orders.\n\n- stepId is just the merkle root (`Step` itself), letting the same root be referenced offchain without\n  per-chain rederivation.\n- pathId is the path's merkle leaf hash. Because `Path` carries `chainId`, the leaf — and therefore\n  pathId — already binds to a specific chain. Gateway rejects paths whose `chainId` does not match\n  the executing chain.\n- A step root can be reused across chains by construction. Path IDs only match across chains when\n  the same `chainId` is deliberately encoded in the path, which Gateway prevents from executing on\n  the wrong chain.\n\n*/\n\nlibrary StepLib {\n    function id(Step step) internal pure returns (bytes32) {\n        return Step.unwrap(step);\n    }\n}\n\nlibrary PathLib {\n    function id(Path calldata path) internal pure returns (bytes32) {\n        return id(path.chainId, path.salt, path.executor, keccak256(path.message));\n    }\n\n    /// @dev Component form, for callers that hold a message hash rather than a `Path` (e.g. the destination\n    ///      stepId derivation in the counterfactual source executors).\n    function id(uint256 chainId, bytes32 salt, bytes32 executor, bytes32 messageHash) internal pure returns (bytes32) {\n        return keccak256(abi.encode(chainId, salt, executor, messageHash));\n    }\n}\n"},{"file_path":"lib/openzeppelin-contracts/contracts/utils/cryptography/MessageHashUtils.sol","source_code":"// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\n// OpenZeppelin Contracts (last updated v5.3.0) (utils/cryptography/MessageHashUtils.sol)\n\npragma solidity ^0.8.20;\n\nimport {Strings} from \"../Strings.sol\";\n\n/**\n * @dev Signature message hash utilities for producing digests to be consumed by {ECDSA} recovery or signing.\n *\n * The library provides methods for generating a hash of a message that conforms to the\n * https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-191[ERC-191] and https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-712[EIP 712]\n * specifications.\n */\nlibrary MessageHashUtils {\n    /**\n     * @dev Returns the keccak256 digest of an ERC-191 signed data with version\n     * `0x45` (`personal_sign` messages).\n     *\n     * The digest is calculated by prefixing a bytes32 `messageHash` with\n     * `\"\\x19Ethereum Signed Message:\\n32\"` and hashing the result.
